title: Primitive Clumping (Lack of Parameter Object)
pattern: A set of primitives (such as start and end dates, or coordinate pairs) are consistently passed together through multiple functions but are never formalised into a single type.
why_bad: It leads to long, unreadable parameter lists and invites errors (such as swapping start and end parameters). In addition, it fails to provide a logical home for verification rules (e.g., checking that `end_date >= start_date`).
detection: Multiple function signatures throughout the code repeat the same sequence of primitive type parameters.
counterexample: Functions that happen to take similar primitives but have no shared semantic relationship (e.g., `(user_id: u32, timeout: u32)`).
